chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Salama Sahib al-Sabiri, from Abu al-Sabbah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Indeed, Allah — Blessed and Exalted — says: The fast is for Me, and I shall recompense upon it.

key_terms.أَجْزِي: ajzi: I recompense/reward — used here in the first person Divine, underscoring that God's reward is personal and immeasurable
key_terms.الصَّوْم: sawm: fasting, the complete abstention from food, drink, and other nullifiers from dawn to sunset as an act of worship
key_terms.تَبَارَكَ وَتَعَالَى: Tabaraka wa-ta'ala: Blessed and Exalted — an honorific formula affirming God's transcendence

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq narrate about Allah's special reward for fasting?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) transmits a Divine hadith (hadith qudsi) in which God declares that fasting is uniquely and exclusively dedicated to Him and that He Himself will directly reward the fasting person. Unlike other acts of worship whose rewards are quantified, God's direct recompense for fasting signals its extraordinary spiritual status. The statement 'the fast is for Me' was understood by classical scholars as indicating that fasting — unlike salat or zakat — has no ostensible, outward expression by which a person may seek worldly praise, making it a uniquely sincere act of devotion.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Salma Sahib Al Sabiry, from Abu Al Sabbah, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Blessed and High is Saying: “The Fast is for Me<sup>azwj</sup>, and I<sup>azwj</sup> shall Recompense upon it’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Salamah, Sahib al-Sabiriy from abu al-Sabbah who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that
Allah, the most Blessed, the most High, has said, ‘Fasting is for Me, and I reward for it.’”
